invariantAllocations.invariant: Program Kit-owned C# changed by the integration and release-provenance implementation satisfies the current private repository source-quality policy.
invariantAllocations.rationale: The existing private analyzer and build spine already enforce Program Kit C# structure and build-time quality constraints.

invariantAllocations.invariant: Pull-request and merge-queue checks execute against GitHub's combined source and report one stable required-check result without publication authority.
invariantAllocations.rationale: Event payloads, synthetic merge commits, permissions, concurrency, and required-check reporting are workflow behavior and cannot be proven by a C# analyzer.

invariantAllocations.invariant: Only a successful push run for protected main creates a publication-eligible package set bound to exact source, workflow, manifest, and package digests.
invariantAllocations.rationale: Build-run provenance, hosted-runner state, artifact storage, attestations, and exact package bytes require executable CI and artifact verification.

invariantAllocations.invariant: Human-dispatched publication selects one exact eligible main build, verifies it, and publishes those bytes without restore, build, test, or pack.
invariantAllocations.rationale: Workflow authority, protected environments, temporary credentials, artifact retrieval, and registry side effects are dynamic execution boundaries.

invariantAllocations.invariant: Repository settings, publication approval, semantic design approval, and material compatibility decisions remain human-owned.
invariantAllocations.rationale: Neither source analyzers nor workflows may originate human authority or silently change repository and environment policy.

rationale: The existing private Program Kit C# gate remains compatible with all applicable Program Kit-owned implementation source. GitHub event semantics, combined commits, workflow permissions, package provenance, artifact retrieval, protected publication, and external registry effects remain executable and human-review obligations. No new analyzer or gate extension is justified.
residualRisks: Hosted CI and artifact storage remain external services whose availability is not guaranteed by repository source.
NuGet publication of a coordinated multi-package set is not atomic; a transport failure can leave a partial external publication requiring explicit human recovery.
Repository rulesets, merge queue, protected environments, and trusted-publishing policy require human configuration outside the commit.
nonStaticClaims: Pull-request merge refs, merge-group commits, event payloads, permissions, cancellation, and status reporting require workflow execution.
Package inventory, archive bytes, checksums, build-run identity, source commit, artifact attestations, and no-rebuild publication require executable provenance checks.
External package-feed acceptance, GitHub release creation, and protected-environment approval require separately authorized external execution.
